```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>")
```

This walkthrough constructs a treatment specification, runs the truth layer,
and explains the resulting cohort and treatment-effect tables. One fixed-course
example is evaluated when the vignette is built. The subsequent strategy
variations are optional code examples that you can run separately.

The example assigns a 365-day aspirin course after first myocardial infarction
(MI). The duration is a demonstration of a simulator rule. It is not a claim
that this schedule or the configured hazard coefficients have been clinically
validated.

## Choose a treatment rule

| Function | Rule |
|---|---|
| `truth_persistent_course_treatment()` | Start at a qualifying event and continue, optionally stopping at a later event. |
| `truth_fixed_course_treatment()` | Give one course, with an optional initiation delay and event-triggered stopping. |
| `truth_episodic_course_treatment()` | Allow qualifying events to begin further courses, with optional restarting after a stop. |

Each call reproduces the complete practice simulation using the supplied
inputs. The layer retains the P7 hazard histories and continues through P13 to
check that the eligible patients are observable in the analyst-visible EHR at
time zero. You do not need to source the pipeline scripts or run
`simulate_one_gp()` first.

```{r practice-inputs}
library(EHRSim)
inputs <- list(pracid = 1L, gp_rel_size = 1, seed = 34637L)
```

Practice size is relative rather than an exact patient count. Changing these
inputs defines a different simulation. For a matching EHR run, retain the same
inputs, package version and software environment.

## Define the fixed course

```{r fixed-specification}
fixed_specs <- list(
  strategy_type = "fixed_course_once",
  drug_name = "aspirin",
  population = "first_mi_aspirin_naive",
  start_trigger_label = "first_mi",
  start_trigger_cols = "mi_event_first_date",
  time_zero_col = "first_mi_date",
  course_duration_days = 365L,
  course_delay_days = 0L,
  stop_trigger_labels = c("upper_gi_bleed", "peptic_ulcer"),
  stop_trigger_cols = c(
    "upper_gi_bleed_event_date",
    "peptic_ulcer_event_date"
  ),
  affected_cause = "non_communicable_death",
  affected_hazard_column = "lnhr_all_1",
  horizons = c(1, 5, 10)
)
```

The fields have different roles:

| Field | What it controls |
|---|---|
| `drug_name` | The selected treatment group and configured prescription coefficients. |
| `start_trigger_cols` | Existing disease-date columns used to find the earliest qualifying event. |
| `time_zero_col` | The name assigned to that derived event date. The engine creates this column. |
| `population`, `start_trigger_label` | Descriptive labels for the cohort and trigger. They do not apply a custom patient filter. |
| `course_duration_days`, `course_delay_days` | The scheduled course length and initiation delay, both in days. |
| `stop_trigger_cols`, `stop_trigger_labels` | Stopping dates and matching descriptive labels. Supply both fields together or omit both. |
| `affected_hazard_column` | The hazard modified by the treatment coefficient. `lnhr_all_1` represents non-communicable mortality. |
| `affected_cause` | A label describing the modified component; changing it alone does not switch hazards. |
| `horizons` | Follow-up times in years, independently of course duration. |

The simulator must contain the named trigger columns and the selected
treatment's coefficients. A new drug name or population label does not add a
new drug model or eligibility rule. The help page gives the full input
reference:

```{r function-help, eval=FALSE}
?truth_fixed_course_treatment
```

## Run and inspect the cohort

```{r run-fixed-course, results='hide', message=FALSE, warning=FALSE}
fixed_truth <- truth_fixed_course_treatment(
  pracid = inputs$pracid,
  gp_rel_size = inputs$gp_rel_size,
  seed = inputs$seed,
  specs = fixed_specs
)
```

The eligible cohort consists of patients with a qualifying MI date, no
prescription of the selected treatment group before that date, and EHR
observability at that date. Same-day first treatment is allowed. Registration,
transfer, linked death and study end determine observability, with endpoint
dates included. A recorded MI diagnosis code is not required for entry.

This is the package's default eligible cohort. If you subsequently apply
additional filters to analyst-visible EHR data, this default truth population
does not automatically become that separately selected analysis cohort.

```{r eligible-patients}
nrow(fixed_truth$eligible)
schedule <- as.data.frame(fixed_truth$eligible)[, c(
  "patient_id", "time_zero", "course_start_date",
  "planned_course_end", "actual_course_end"
), drop = FALSE]
knitr::kable(
  head(schedule), row.names = FALSE,
  col.names = c("Patient", "Time zero", "Course start", "Planned end", "Stopping end")
)
```

`planned_course_end` is 365 days after scheduled initiation.
`actual_course_end` describes the stopping version: it also accounts for the
first qualifying stop and the retained follow-up boundary. It is not the
course end used in every returned world.

Because the specification includes stopping events, the engine constructs two
versions. `fixed_course_no_stopping` ignores those events but still ends at the
scheduled course end. `fixed_course_with_stopping` can end sooner at an event.
Both are compared with assigned no aspirin in the same eligible patients.

## Read the treatment effects

```{r effect-summary}
effects <- fixed_truth$truth_treatment_effects
summary <- as.data.frame(effects$contrast_population)
summary <- summary[, c(
  "truth_version", "horizon_years", "n_patients", "n_complete",
  "mean_survival_diff", "mean_risk_diff", "mean_rmst_days_diff"
), drop = FALSE]
knitr::kable(
  summary, digits = 3, row.names = FALSE,
  col.names = c("Stopping rule", "Horizon (years)", "Patients", "Complete",
                "Survival difference", "Risk difference", "RMST difference (days)")
)
```

Each row is assigned treatment minus assigned no treatment, for one stopping
version and one requested horizon. The natural treatment history is an
additional reference; it is not the comparator in this main contrast table.

| Column | Interpretation |
|---|---|
| `n_patients` | Patients represented in the constructed contrast table. |
| `n_complete` | Patients whose retained hazard follow-up covers the full horizon and contributes to the mean effect. |
| `mean_survival_diff` | Difference in all-cause survival probability. |
| `mean_risk_diff` | Difference in all-cause death risk. |
| `mean_rmst_days_diff` | Difference in restricted mean survival time (RMST), in days. Positive values mean longer expected survival under the assigned treatment rule. |

RMST is expected survival time accumulated up to the selected horizon. The
treatment modifies one mortality component, while these survival, risk and
RMST summaries use the combined all-cause mortality hazard.
A negative risk difference means lower simulated death risk under treatment.
Multiply a probability difference by 100 to express it in percentage points.

Check `n_complete` before comparing horizons. The current engine averages
full-horizon effects only for patients with sufficient retained hazard
follow-up. The 1-, 5- and 10-year rows can therefore describe different subsets.
If no patients contribute, a summary mean can be `NaN`, which means no
contributors rather than no treatment effect.

Stopping and no-stopping results can be identical if there are no relevant
stopping events during the active courses in the contributing subset. A
stopping rule does not guarantee that the generated population exercises it.

The coefficient table shows the configured hazard ratio while treatment is
active:

```{r configured-coefficients}
coefficient_summary <- as.data.frame(effects$coefficients)[, c(
  "truth_version", "drug", "log_hr_while_active", "hr_while_active", "hr_inactive"
), drop = FALSE]
knitr::kable(
  coefficient_summary, digits = 3, row.names = FALSE,
  col.names = c("Stopping rule", "Drug", "Active log-HR", "Active HR", "Inactive HR")
)
```

The hazard ratio is an input to the simulator, whereas the RMST difference
depends on that coefficient together with the population's hazard histories,
treatment schedules and horizon. The two quantities are not interchangeable.

## Inspect additional output

| Returned object | Use |
|---|---|
| `eligible` | Check who entered the cohort and their time zero. |
| `treatment_cohort` | Inspect follow-up intervals and exposure flags. |
| `truth_worlds` | Inspect natural, assigned-treatment and assigned-no-treatment interval histories. |
| `truth_treatment_effects$contrast_patient` | Inspect individual full-horizon contrasts. |
| `truth_treatment_effects$horizon_patient` | Inspect each patient's follow-up completeness, survival, risk and RMST. |
| `truth_treatment_effects$survival_curve_mean` | Inspect mean survival by grid time and the number contributing. |
| `truth_treatment_effects$metadata` | Inspect the estimand labels and cohort basis. |
| `truth_treatment_effects$coefficients` | Inspect the treatment coefficients used. |

Shared natural and no-treatment reference histories are returned once in the
cleaned interval outputs. Use the provided contrast tables, which retain both
stopping versions, instead of manually joining those cleaned worlds by version.

```{r inspect-more, eval=FALSE}
effects$metadata
head(effects$horizon_patient)
head(effects$survival_curve_mean)
```

## Adapt the specification

The following changes reuse the specification. Each function call runs a new
simulation; run the variations individually when exploring them.

### Omit event-triggered stopping

```{r omit-stopping, eval=FALSE}
no_stop_specs <- fixed_specs
no_stop_specs$stop_trigger_cols <- NULL
no_stop_specs$stop_trigger_labels <- NULL
no_stop_truth <- truth_fixed_course_treatment(
  pracid = inputs$pracid, gp_rel_size = inputs$gp_rel_size,
  seed = inputs$seed, specs = no_stop_specs
)
```

Removing both stop fields produces only the no-stopping version. The fixed
course still ends at its scheduled end.

### Delay initiation by 30 days

```{r delayed-course, eval=FALSE}
delayed_specs <- fixed_specs
delayed_specs$strategy_type <- "fixed_course_delayed"
delayed_specs$course_delay_days <- 30L
delayed_truth <- truth_fixed_course_treatment(
  pracid = inputs$pracid, gp_rel_size = inputs$gp_rel_size,
  seed = inputs$seed, specs = delayed_specs
)
```

Eligibility and follow-up remain anchored at MI; treatment starts 30 days
later. Patients are not selected for surviving until initiation. A stopping
event during the delay can prevent treatment from becoming active in the
stopping version. Setting the type label alone would not introduce the delay.

### Continue treatment persistently

```{r persistent-treatment, eval=FALSE}
persistent_specs <- fixed_specs
persistent_specs[c("strategy_type", "start_trigger_cols",
                   "course_duration_days", "course_delay_days")] <- NULL
persistent_specs$start_trigger_col <- "mi_event_first_date"
persistent_specs$strategy_context_label <- "after_first_mi"
persistent_truth <- truth_persistent_course_treatment(
  pracid = inputs$pracid, gp_rel_size = inputs$gp_rel_size,
  seed = inputs$seed, specs = persistent_specs
)
```

The persistent wrapper uses the singular `start_trigger_col` and requires
`strategy_context_label`. It begins treatment at the trigger and continues
through retained follow-up, optionally stopping at a qualifying event. This
family does not restart after a stop.

### Allow episodic courses and restarting

```{r episodic-treatment, eval=FALSE}
episodic_specs <- fixed_specs
episodic_specs$strategy_type <- "episodic_course_restart"
episodic_specs$restart_after_stop <- TRUE
episodic_specs$population <- "first_vascular_event_aspirin_naive"
episodic_specs$start_trigger_label <- "first_vascular_event"
episodic_specs$start_trigger_cols <- c(
  "mi_event_first_date", "stroke_event_first_date", "chd_onset_date",
  "pvd_onset_date", "other_athero_onset_date"
)
episodic_specs$time_zero_col <- "first_vascular_event_date"
episodic_truth <- truth_episodic_course_treatment(
  pracid = inputs$pracid, gp_rel_size = inputs$gp_rel_size,
  seed = inputs$seed, specs = episodic_specs
)
head(episodic_truth$episode_triggers)
```

The broader trigger set changes the eligible population. Its earliest date
defines time zero; later available trigger dates can start further courses.
First-MI and first-stroke columns do not represent every recurrent event.

With `restart_after_stop = TRUE`, a course takes its first stopping event at
or after its scheduled start and before its planned end. The same event can
stop several overlapping courses. A later trigger can start another course.
Overlapping active courses still give binary treatment exposure, not extra
doses or a multiplied effect.

To retain stopping without restarting, set both
`strategy_type = "episodic_course_one_stop"` and `restart_after_stop = FALSE`.
The first qualifying patient-level stop then applies across later courses.

To use the first of several triggers for just one course, pass the broader
trigger set to the fixed-course wrapper with
`strategy_type = "multi_trigger_fixed_course"`. The function family, trigger
columns and restart flag determine the mechanism, rather than a descriptive
label alone.

## Relate truth to the EHR and retain a run record

Generate the matching analyst-visible EHR with the same practice inputs:

```{r matching-ehr, eval=FALSE}
ehr <- simulate_one_gp(
  pracid = inputs$pracid, gp_rel_size = inputs$gp_rel_size,
  seed = inputs$seed, write_csv = FALSE
)
```

The treatment wrappers rebuild the simulation themselves. They do not read
the `ehr` object or a saved CSV folder. Transfer after time zero ends EHR
observation; it does not automatically terminate the latent assigned strategy.

The wrapper returns results in memory. To save a result and its settings,
explicitly run:

```{r save-run, eval=FALSE, purl=FALSE}
saveRDS(
  list(
    inputs = inputs,
    specs = fixed_specs,
    package_description = packageDescription("EHRSim"),
    session = sessionInfo(),
    result = fixed_truth
  ),
  file = "fixed_course_aspirin_run.rds"
)
```

`package_description` records the package version and the Git commit field
when installed from GitHub. `session` records R and loaded package versions.
The RDS file is written to the current working directory.

## Scope and practical checks

These contrasts are conditional on retained patient and hazard histories.
The treatment layer changes exposure and mortality hazards but does not
regenerate disease dates, other trajectories or trigger events under each
intervention. Scientific calibration and estimator-recovery studies require
additional evidence.

If the eligible cohort is empty, the wrapper gives an explicit error. A larger
practice or different seed may produce eligible patients, but also changes the
simulation. For missing-trigger or missing-coefficient errors, check names
against the bundled model; changing a descriptive label cannot add the missing
mechanism. Consult the detailed function help for supported fields:

```{r other-help, eval=FALSE}
?truth_persistent_course_treatment
?truth_episodic_course_treatment
```
